name: Hanuman Dhoka Royal Palace
description: The palace grew across successive Malla, Shah and Rana reigns, turning a royal residence into a layered record of government, ceremony and craft.
lookFor: Read the changing brick, timber and neoclassical fronts as additions rather than one uniform building.
photoPrompt: Make a wide exterior portrait that shows two architectural periods in one frame.

name: Hanuman Gate
description: Pratap Malla placed the red-cloaked image of Hanuman beside the palace entrance, giving Hanuman Dhoka its enduring name and a guardian at the royal threshold.
lookFor: Notice how the sacred guardian, gate and flow of visitors share a very small threshold.
photoPrompt: Photograph your group beside—not touching—the gateway, leaving the guardian fully visible.

name: Nasal Chowk
description: Nasal Chowk carried royal ceremony from the Malla era into the modern monarchy; coronations continued here through 2001.
lookFor: Stand at the edge and trace how balconies turn an inward courtyard into a theatre of state.
photoPrompt: Create a symmetrical courtyard photograph from a permitted public position.

name: Mohan Chowk
description: Mohan Chowk was an inward royal residence where access, water and ritual were tightly controlled within the palace.
lookFor: Look for the repeated carved window rhythm and the way every side faces the court.
photoPrompt: Count one façade's window bays and record the number with a note; do not enter closed areas.

name: Sundari Chowk
description: Pratap Malla's Sundari Chowk joined courtly beauty to an intensely private royal world inside Hanuman Dhoka.
lookFor: Compare its enclosed scale with the open public square outside the palace walls.
photoPrompt: Write a short contrast between the enclosed court and the public square; respect palace photography signs.

name: Basantapur Durbar (Nine-Storey Palace)
description: The Nine-Storey Palace rose after the Shah conquest and linked four tower names—Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, Lalitpur and Kirtipur—to a new royal centre.
lookFor: Follow the tower upward through diminishing storeys and changing window scale.
photoPrompt: Take a vertical personal portrait that keeps the full tower above you without blocking the path.

name: Taleju Bhawani Temple
description: Mahendra Malla's high Taleju temple made the royal goddess visible over the city while keeping the sanctuary exceptionally restricted.
lookFor: Observe the twelve-stage plinth and 36.6-metre vertical rise only from an allowed public viewpoint.
photoPrompt: Frame the temple above surrounding roofs from outside; never ask to enter or photograph a restricted ritual.

name: Degu Taleju Temple
description: Degu Taleju faced Pratap Malla's column across the royal square, joining palace worship to a deliberately composed public axis.
lookFor: Find the line between the praying king on his column and the temple he faces.
photoPrompt: Capture the column–temple sightline without stepping into worship or traffic.

name: Panchamukhi Hanuman Temple
description: Pratap Malla's Panchamukhi Hanuman temple places the five-faced protective form within Nasal Chowk's palace world.
lookFor: Study the tiered silhouette from a permitted area; the sacred interior is not a photo target.
photoPrompt: Sketch or describe the roof silhouette instead of photographing any restricted interior.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: The Jagannath image was installed under Mahendra Malla; the temple's carved timber struts also preserve frank scenes of worldly life.
lookFor: Examine the structural role and narrative detail of the struts without treating sacred carving as a joke.
photoPrompt: Photograph one full timber strut in context, avoiding intrusive close-ups of worshippers.

name: Mahendreshwar Temple
description: Mahendra Malla's Shiva temple is one of the foundations that established the square's dense sixteenth-century sacred landscape.
lookFor: Notice how a smaller shrine holds its ground beside much larger royal monuments.
photoPrompt: Make a scale photograph with the temple and a consenting companion at a respectful distance.

name: Kotilingeshwar Temple
description: Kotilingeshwar belongs to Mahendra Malla's temple-building campaign and the square's closely spaced Shaiva shrines.
lookFor: Look for the linga dedication and how offerings keep a historic structure in present use.
photoPrompt: Record an exterior detail that shows living worship without photographing a person at prayer.

name: Krishna Temple
description: Pratap Malla built the octagonal Krishna temple in memory of two queens, turning private loss into a public royal monument.
lookFor: Walk around its many-sided plan and notice how no single façade gives the whole building.
photoPrompt: Take three exterior frames from different sides and choose the one that best explains the octagon.

name: Kal Bhairav
description: The monumental black Bhairav made Shiva's fierce form a public focus of oath, justice and worship in the royal square.
lookFor: Observe scale, gesture and the open-air relationship between deity and crowd.
photoPrompt: Make a respectful group photograph from the edge, with everyone consenting and no offerings blocked.

name: Swet Bhairav
description: Swet Bhairav remains concealed for most of the year and is revealed during Indra Jatra, making limited visibility part of the monument's meaning.
lookFor: When closed, study the screen and threshold rather than trying to defeat the restriction.
photoPrompt: Photograph the closed exterior or write what seasonal access teaches; never push through a ritual crowd.

name: Narsingha Statue
description: Pratap Malla erected Vishnu's man-lion form in 1673; its inscription ties royal performance, fear and atonement to a single forceful image.
lookFor: Read the dramatic movement of protector, victim and carved stone as one composition.
photoPrompt: Recreate the statue's strong diagonal only with your camera angle—never climb or touch it.

name: Pratap Malla Stone Column
description: The king kneels above the square facing Taleju, presenting royal authority as devotion rather than a freestanding portrait.
lookFor: Follow the figure's gaze to understand why the column stands where it does.
photoPrompt: Capture the full column and the temple it faces in one alignment study.

name: Kumari Ghar
description: Kumari Ghar is both an extraordinary carved courtyard and the present residence of Kathmandu's living goddess, revered by Buddhist and Hindu communities.
lookFor: Study the exterior and courtyard woodwork while remembering that this is a child's home, not a performance set.
photoPrompt: Photograph only the architecture. Do not photograph the Kumari or any child, and ask consent before including people.

name: Kasthamandap (Maru Sattal)
description: Kasthamandap gave Kathmandu its name, collapsed catastrophically in 2015, and was rebuilt through a community-led process using salvaged historic fabric where possible.
lookFor: Distinguish reused carved timber from new replacement work without assuming age from colour alone.
photoPrompt: Create a then-and-now-minded exterior record and note one old-looking and one new-looking element.

name: Simha Sattal
description: Simha Sattal extends the square's heritage beyond temples: open rest houses supported trade, encounter, shelter and festival life.
lookFor: Notice the open ground floor and how a civic building receives people rather than enclosing them.
photoPrompt: Take a candid-free wide view showing the building's public function; blur or exclude faces when possible.

name: Maju Dega
description: Maju Dega's tall stepped plinth long served as both sacred base and public lookout; its 2015 collapse changed the square's skyline before reconstruction restored the form.
lookFor: Count how the broad steps lift the temple above everyday movement.
photoPrompt: Take a personal portrait from ground level with the steps behind you; do not climb where access is closed.

name: Shiva–Parvati Temple
description: Shiva and Parvati lean from an upper window toward the square, turning a domestic-looking façade into a divine observation point.
lookFor: Find the figures above before studying the carved windows below.
photoPrompt: Make a playful group frame looking upward like the divine couple, keeping the path clear.

name: Ashok Vinayak (Kathmandu Ganesh)
description: Ashok Vinayak is a compact, intensely active Ganesh shrine whose importance comes from continuing worship rather than monumental size.
lookFor: Notice the unusual roofless or low-canopy presence and the constant negotiation between shrine and street.
photoPrompt: Record a written sound-and-movement observation instead of aiming a camera at worshippers.

name: Kabindrapur
description: Kabindrapur is counted among Pratap Malla's monuments and helps reveal how royal patronage filled the square with distinct but interdependent shrines.
lookFor: Find one carved feature that distinguishes it from its nearest neighbour.
photoPrompt: Photograph the distinguishing feature and name it in one sentence.

name: Indrapur Temple
description: Indrapur connects the royal square to Indra, rain, kingship and the festival cycle that periodically transforms Kathmandu's streets.
lookFor: Look for signs that the monument participates in a route larger than its footprint.
photoPrompt: Take a route-context photo showing the temple and the street continuing beyond it.

name: Gaddi Baithak
description: Chandra Shumsher's white neoclassical audience hall deliberately interrupts the brick-and-timber Malla setting, recording a later court's global architectural ambitions.
lookFor: Compare columns, arches and white plaster with the carved Newar buildings opposite.
photoPrompt: Split the frame between Gaddi Baithak and a traditional façade for an architecture comparison.

name: Trailokya Mohan Narayan Temple
description: Trailokya Mohan's collapse in 2015 exposed how much of a temple's identity depends on recovered timber, remembered ritual and its place in the square.
lookFor: Study joints, fresh brick and older carved elements as evidence of reconstruction.
photoPrompt: Record one junction between old and new-looking fabric without crossing barriers.

name: Gopinath Temple
description: Gopinath adds another Vaishnava dedication to an ensemble where similar divine names belong to separate foundations, communities and histories.
lookFor: Identify it by position and form rather than assuming every Narayan-related shrine is the same.
photoPrompt: Make an identification photo including the temple and one fixed neighbouring landmark.

name: Saraswati Temple
description: The Saraswati shrine honours learning and music; reconstruction after the earthquake returned a small but meaningful element to the square's sacred network.
lookFor: Notice musical or learning associations in offerings and iconography without disturbing them.
photoPrompt: Write three visual details that suggest the dedication; use a photo only when worship is not underway.

name: Laxmi Narayan Temple
description: Laxmi and Narayan unite prosperity and preservation within a temple restored after the 2015 earthquake.
lookFor: Compare restored brick and timber surfaces for different weathering patterns.
photoPrompt: Take a material-study close-up that excludes faces, offerings and restricted interiors.

name: Chyasin Dega
description: Chyasin Dega's eight-sided plan makes movement essential to understanding it; recovered elements were repaired and returned during reconstruction.
lookFor: Walk a legal circuit and count the changing faces of the octagon.
photoPrompt: Capture a four-image sequence from alternating sides, or record the count if photography is crowded.

name: Tarini Devi Temple (Tarini Bahal)
description: Tarini Bahal's conservation was led through community and municipal support under Department of Archaeology oversight, showing stewardship beyond the palace administration.
lookFor: Notice what makes the place feel locally maintained rather than museum-contained.
photoPrompt: Record one sign of community care and explain it in a note.

name: Dashain Ghar
description: Dashain Ghar belongs to the ritual infrastructure of Nepal's major autumn festival, when palace spaces and public authority are temporarily reordered.
lookFor: Read doors and controlled thresholds as signs of seasonal use, not as invitations.
photoPrompt: Photograph only the public exterior and describe how a closed building can remain culturally active.

name: Nagara Ghar
description: Nagara Ghar supported ceremonial sound, reminding us that the heritage of the square was heard as well as seen.
lookFor: Pause for one minute and separate bells, voices, traffic and ritual sounds.
photoPrompt: Submit a written sound map with at least four sounds; no photograph required.

name: Dhukuti Ghar
description: Dhukuti Ghar represents the palace's practical treasury and storage functions, the less visible systems that sustained royal ceremony.
lookFor: Compare its defensive, contained character with the display-oriented façades nearby.
photoPrompt: Make a texture study of the public exterior without attempting access.

name: Dasavatar Temple
description: The Dasavatar dedication gathers Vishnu's ten descents into one narrative framework, joining architecture to a cycle of stories.
lookFor: Identify how repeated niches or images organize multiple episodes.
photoPrompt: Choose one visible narrative panel, photograph it in context and write what remains uncertain.

name: Natyeshwar Temple
description: Natyeshwar links sacred space with dance and performance, arts that activate the palace beyond static architecture.
lookFor: Find a carved posture or rhythm and follow its line with your eyes.
photoPrompt: With consent, make a solo silhouette echoing one visible pose from a respectful distance.

name: Kageshwar Temple
description: Kageshwar is another named shrine in the restored Hanuman Dhoka ensemble, part of the density that earns the square its 'museum of temples' description.
lookFor: Notice how its roofline overlaps neighbouring monuments from different positions.
photoPrompt: Find a viewpoint where three rooflines layer without hiding Kageshwar.

name: Tribhuvan Gallery and Museum
description: Royal rooms became museum galleries, changing private objects and spaces into a public account of the Shah monarchy.
lookFor: Distinguish the historic room from the later exhibition layer and follow current museum photo rules.
photoPrompt: Write about one object–room relationship; use a photo only where museum signs explicitly allow it.

name: Shisha Baithak
description: Shisha Baithak displays a Malla throne within a later palace presentation, compressing dynasties and curatorial choices into one viewing space.
lookFor: Ask what belongs to the original setting and what was arranged later for visitors.
photoPrompt: Record a note separating object, architecture and exhibition; follow all indoor photo restrictions.
